Meanwhile the delivery’s later batches wait in this destination’s buffer of
batches, which drops its oldest when full. With a store, the records of a dropped batch aren’t
lost: once the destination has caught up, the delivery reads them back from the store and sends

gives how many records were dropped, when they were tracked, and how many of them a store keeps
to send again. Drops no one has read yet merge into one report per destination, so a report may
count several batches. The delivery logs each drop too. Its reports end once the delivery is
gone, and a delivery built to replace one has reports of its own. One task reads them at a time,
as with every report stream the library hands out: a second reader waits its turn.

The enricher runs as the delivery hands each batch to that destination, so it reaches every record
the destination receives, however the event was tracked: through any copy of the tracker, from a
detached task handed the tracker, or recovered by a store after a relaunch. That makes it the place
for values about the destination or the delivery, such as a region or a deployment tag, and not for
values about the event. A record recovered after a relaunch would get this run’s app version, and
the network connection at upload rather than when it was tracked, so keep the standard context

abstract.text: Give views the tracker the way each framework passes values down, and let modifiers and controls track what views do.
Run a test’s body with a fresh tracker and check the events it tracked.
Typed analytics events for Swift, delivered in batches to any number of destinations.
Send each batch of records to an HTTP endpoint, and send it again until it arrives.
A destination that writes each tracked event to a swift-log
Send events to an analytics vendor Traffluent doesn’t cover yet, from a module of your own, with the same rules as the destinations it ships.
Add Traffluent to an app, declare its events, deliver them to a server and test what the app tracks.
A destination that adds each tracked event to the span that was active when it was tracked.
Deliver an event only once the user grants the purpose it is collected for.
Write batches of records in TraffluentCollector’s ingest format, for an
protocol, the modifiers that narrow what a destination receives, and the delivery that hands it batches.
Send records to PostHog Cloud or a self-hosted PostHog through its batch capture API.
Keep each record on disk until it is delivered, so a record the app tracked survives the process ending.
